AgentRunConfig.description:
Optional per-role or per-company overrides for agent run limits and retrieval tuning.

Values are applied in precedence order:  {@link  TcpRole.runConfig  }  →  {@link  TcpCompany.runConfig  }  → environment variables → code defaults. Any field left undefined falls through to the next level.

maxIterations.description: Maximum number of LLM invocations before the run is cancelled as failed.

maxQaAttempts.description: Maximum QA rejections a task assignment may accrue before it fails.

ragThreshold.description: Minimum cosine similarity (0–1) a knowledge chunk must score to be retrieved. Set per role/company when an embedding model's score distribution differs from the default's — see  {@link  DEFAULT_RAG_THRESHOLD  } .

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock timeout in milliseconds before the run is cancelled as failed.

AgentStatus.description: Lifecycle states for an agent instance.

AuditEvent.description: A single entry in the audit log for an agent run. Rows are written by lcp-agent as it processes LangGraph events. The composite index on `(companyId, agentId, timestamp)` supports efficient time-ordered queries and live-stream reads per ADR-008.

agent.description: The agent that produced this event. Nullable for system-level events.

agentId.description: Foreign key for the  {@link  TcpAgent }  that produced this event.

assignmentId.description: Denormalised copy of the producing agent's assignment at write time (see  {@link  TcpAssignment.parentAssignmentId  }  for why assignments now always carry a task-traceable lineage). No relation object — like `agentId`, this is a plain column so hot-path writes never risk an accidental join.

company.description: The company context for this event.

companyId.description: Foreign key for the owning  {@link  TcpCompany } .

payload.description:
Structured event payload. Content varies by  {@link  AuditEventType } :
- `llm_request` / `llm_response`: message content and token counts
- `tool_call` / `tool_result`: tool name, input, and output
- `decision`: summary and justification
- `state_change`: reason and new status

role.description: The role name at the time of the event (denormalised for query convenience since the role may be updated after the run).

taskId.description: Denormalised task scope, derived server-side (from the producing agent's assignment, or supplied explicitly for agent-less orchestrator rows) so it never drifts. Backs `(companyId, taskId, timestamp)` task-history queries.

timestamp.description: When this event was recorded. Defaults to the current time.

AuditEventType.description: Categories of event captured in the audit log (per ADR-008).

CompanyUser.description: A human user associated with a company. Used for query routing (matching conversations to the right user) and for the human-in-the-loop pause/resume flow in Phases 5–6.

companyId.description: The company this user belongs to.

createdAt.description: When this user was added to the company.

identifier.description: OIDC subject (`sub`) claim or email address — unique per company.

knowledgeDomains.description: Knowledge domains this user covers (e.g. `"finance"`, `"legal"`). Used by query routing to prefer the best-matched user.

memberType.description: Membership tier. `creator` is set on company creation and cannot be removed.

ConsultationStatus.description: Lifecycle states for an inter-agent consultation.

Conversation.description:
A question posed by an agent to one or more human users. Created when an agent calls `request_user_input`; closed when a human replies.

The slug is human-readable (`{roleName}-{queryIndex}`) and is the primary identifier used by CLI commands. It is unique per role.

agentId.description: The agent that raised this question.

companyId.description: The company this conversation belongs to.

context.description: Optional additional context provided by the agent alongside the question.

question.description: The question the agent is asking.

roleId.description: The role ID that originated this question.

roleName.description: The role that originated this question (denormalised — kept even if role is later renamed).

routedToIdentifiers.description: OIDC identifiers of the users this question was routed to.

slug.description: Human-readable unique identifier in the form `{role-name}-{queryIndex}`.

ConversationMessage.description: A single message in a  {@link  Conversation  }  thread. Messages are append-only — one `agent` message (the question) followed by zero or one `user` message (the reply that closes the conversation).

author.description: Whether this message was written by the agent or a human user.

authorIdentifier.description: OIDC identifier of the user who replied (null for agent messages).

conversationId.description: The conversation this message belongs to.

EpisodicMemory.description: A single agent-authored memory entry stored for later recall. The embedding vector is stored in a `vector(768)` column managed via raw SQL (pgvector extension) — not mapped by TypeORM.

agentId.description: The agent that recorded this memory (nullable — may be system-generated).

companyId.description: The company that owns this memory.

content.description: Raw text content of the memory.

roleId.description: The role whose episodic memory this belongs to.

KnowledgeChunk.description:
A single chunk of text extracted from an OKF knowledge-base document and stored for RAG retrieval. The corresponding embedding vector is stored directly in PostgreSQL as a `vector(768)` column (pgvector extension) and is not mapped by TypeORM — all vector reads and writes use raw SQL.

Chunks are scoped to a  {@link  TcpCompany  } , and optionally to a  {@link  TcpRole  }  within it — `roleId` is `null` for chunks from the company-wide `knowledge/shared/` folder (see storage-keys.ts). All chunks for a given `documentPath` are replaced atomically on re-index.

chunkIndex.description: Zero-based position of this chunk within its source document.

companyId.description: The company that owns this chunk.

content.description: Raw text content of this chunk.

documentPath.description: MinIO path of the OKF source document this chunk was extracted from. Used to identify all chunks belonging to one document for deletion/re-index.

roleId.description: The role whose knowledge base this chunk belongs to. `null` for chunks indexed from the company-wide `knowledge/shared/` folder.

KnowledgeIndexState.description:
Tracks the RAG-indexing state of a single knowledge *scope* — either a role's `knowledge/{role_slug}/` folder or a company's `knowledge/shared/` folder (when `roleId` is `null`).

Used to keep embeddings in sync with storage (see `apps/lcp-server/src/rag/knowledge-reindex.service.ts`):

- `generation` is a monotonically increasing counter bumped on every change   to the scope. A rebuild job carries the generation it was enqueued with;   the worker skips a job whose generation is older than the current one, and   aborts/re-enqueues if the generation changes mid-rebuild. This gives   restart-on-change semantics without half-indexed state.
- `fingerprint` is a hash of the scope's storage listing recorded at the end   of the last successful rebuild. The reconciliation poller compares it   against a freshly computed fingerprint to detect out-of-band edits (e.g. a   user editing directly in the MinIO console) and trigger a rebuild.

Uniqueness is enforced per scope via two partial unique indexes because a plain `UNIQUE(companyId, roleId)` treats `NULL` role ids as distinct in Postgres, which would allow duplicate shared rows.

companyId.description: The company that owns this knowledge scope.

fingerprint.description: Hash of the storage listing indexed by the last successful rebuild, or `null` if never indexed.

generation.description: Monotonic change counter — bumped on every trigger, carried by rebuild jobs.

lastError.description: Error message from the most recent failed rebuild, or `null` if the last rebuild succeeded (or none has run).

lastErrorAt.description: When  {@link  lastError }  was recorded — absent if it is unset.

roleId.description: The role whose knowledge folder this scope tracks, or `null` for the company-wide `knowledge/shared/` scope.

updatedAt.description: When this scope's state last changed.

LlmConfig.description: Configuration for a specific LLM provider and model. The API key is stored directly in this config object and persisted in the database. Ensure the database has encryption at rest to protect stored keys.

apiKey.description: API key for this provider. Stored in the database as part of the JSONB config block. Masked in API responses when `LCP_MASK_API_KEYS=true` (the default).

baseUrl.description: Base URL override for providers that are not hosted at their default endpoint. Required for `'lm-studio'` (e.g. `'http://localhost:1234/v1'`).

model.description: The model identifier as expected by the provider API (e.g. `'gpt-4o'`, `'qwen3-5b'`).

provider.description: Identifies the provider. Known values: `'lm-studio'` (local OpenAI-compatible endpoint), `'openai'`. Any string value is accepted to support future providers.

timeoutMs.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds for LLM API calls. Defaults to  {@link  DEFAULT_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS  }  when absent. Set higher for slow local models.

MemberType.description: Membership tier for a  {@link  CompanyUser }  within a company.

PendingConsultation.description:
Tracks a paused agent waiting for another agent's consultation response.

Created when an agent calls `request_agent_consultation` via the interactions MCP server. The calling agent is set to  {@link  AgentStatus.Paused  }  until the consultation agent completes and `PauseAndResumeService.completeAgent()` finds this record and re-enqueues the calling agent.

callingAgentId.description: The agent that is paused awaiting the consultation result.

consultationAgentId.description: The newly created agent that will perform the consultation.

result.description: The consultation result written by the consulting agent on completion. Null until the consultation is complete.

TcpAgent.description: A running instance of an  {@link  TcpRole }  within an  {@link  TcpCompany } . Each agent has a LangGraph `thread_id` (stored as  {@link  TcpAgent.threadId } ) that links it to its checkpoint in the PostgreSQL checkpoint store, enabling resumability.

assignment.description: The  {@link  TcpAssignment }  this agent works. Every agent has one — task work uses the task's assignment; plain conversations, API-started agents, and consultations get an auto-created "orphan" assignment. The agent's mode is this assignment's mode (there is no mode column on the agent).

assignmentId.description: Foreign key for the owning  {@link  TcpAssignment } .

company.description: The company this agent belongs to.

companyId.description: Foreign key for the owning  {@link  TcpCompany } .

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this agent record was created.

id.description: Auto-generated primary key. Also used as the LangGraph `thread_id`.

initialPrompt.description: The task prompt supplied when the agent was started.

output.description: Final output produced by the agent on completion. Set from the assignment `summary` on completion (via the tasks service's `complete_assignment`), or as a fallback from the last AI message when the loop exits naturally.

pausedAt.description: Set when this agent transitions to  {@link  AgentStatus.Paused } ; cleared on resume. Scopes which consultation/conversation responses belong to the current pause episode when aggregating a resume message.

requiredToolCalls.description:
Tool names (unprefixed, e.g. `complete_assignment`) that must have been invoked successfully before the agent loop may end. Null means the default (`['complete_assignment']`); an empty array disables enforcement.

Uses `simple-json` (stored as TEXT) for cross-DB compatibility with SQLite unit tests.

role.description: The role template this agent runs as.

roleId.description: Foreign key for the  {@link  TcpRole }  this agent is an instance of.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of this agent.

storageChanges.description:
Storage changes accumulated by the agent loop during the current (or last) run. Updated incrementally by lcp-agent as storage MCP tool calls complete. Used to include context in completion/output-gate error messages.

Uses `simple-json` (stored as TEXT) for cross-DB compatibility with SQLite unit tests.

threadId.description: LangGraph checkpoint thread_id. Set to the agent's own UUID on first run. Null until the first BullMQ job is dispatched.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last status or field update.

TcpArtifact.description: `{ type, value }` pointer to (or literal content of) a single artifact.

TcpArtifactType.description: Where an artifact lives. The three `-path` variants are filenames relative to a location in the task/assignment storage tree (see `storage-keys.ts`); `inline-text` carries literal text directly instead of pointing at storage.

TcpAssignment.description: A unit of work performed by a single agent. Implement-mode assignments belonging to a task, ordered by  {@link  orderIndex } , form that task's plan — there is no separate plan entity. Assignments also exist outside any task ("orphan" assignments — plain conversations/consultations, `taskId: null`) and in `plan`/`qa` modes (the planner's own assignment, and QA review assignments).

agent.description: The agent currently (or last) working this assignment.

approved.description: Set when QA accepts: the artifacts promoted into the assignment's completed directory.

company.description: The company this assignment belongs to — needed directly for orphans.

companyId.description: Foreign key for the owning  {@link  TcpCompany } .

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this assignment was created.

expected.description: Artifacts the assignment is expected to produce.

failureReason.description: Why the assignment failed — QA exhaustion, agent run failure, etc. Null unless `status` is `failed`.

materials.description:
Materials supplied to the assignment.

Uses `simple-json` (stored as TEXT) for cross-DB compatibility with SQLite unit tests.

mode.description: The kind of work this assignment represents.

orderIndex.description:
Position in the task plan. Set only for implement-mode assignments belonging to a task; null for orphans, plan-mode, and qa-mode assignments.

ponytail: a linear plan (one integer per step) is the shipped shape — future DAG-shaped plans (branch/join) replace this with an edge list; `selectNextAssignments` is the intended extension point.

parentAssignment.description: The assignment whose agent spawned this one (e.g. a consultation). Distinct from  {@link  targetAssignment }  (what a QA assignment reviews) — this is "who created me", not "what am I evaluating".

prepared.description: Set by `complete_assignment`: the artifacts the agent prepared for review.

prompt.description: The instructions given to the assigned agent.

qaAttempts.description: Number of QA review cycles this assignment has been through. Never reset.

qaFeedback.description: QA reviewer's feedback. Cleared alongside  {@link  qaStatus } .

qaStatus.description: Outcome of the current/last QA review. Cleared (with  {@link  qaFeedback } ) whenever the assignment (re-)enters `in-progress`.

role.description: The role this assignment must be worked by.

shortcode.description: Short identifier derived from the owning task's shortcode, this assignment's position in the task's plan, and its mode — e.g. `000-000-plan`, `000-001-implement`, `000-001-qa` (see `buildAssignmentShortcode`). Null for orphan assignments (`taskId` null — plain conversations and consultations spawned from one).

status.description: Current lifecycle state of this assignment.

summary.description: The completing agent's final answer, recorded by `complete_assignment`. Becomes the agent's `output` when QA accepts.

targetAssignment.description: qa-mode only: the assignment under review.

task.description: The task this assignment belongs to. Null for orphan assignments.

taskId.description: Foreign key for  {@link  task } . Null for orphan assignments.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last status or field update.

TcpAssignmentCompletedArtifact.description: An artifact promoted into an assignment's completed directory, or inline text.

TcpAssignmentMode.description:
The kind of work an assignment represents. The agent's mode IS its assignment's mode — there is no separate mode column on  {@link  TcpAgent } .

- `plan` — design a task's plan (`create_plan`).
- `implement` — carry out one plan step (`complete_assignment`).
- `qa` — review a completed step (`assure_assignment`).
- `chat` — a conversation with a user (no completion tool).
- `consultee` — answer another agent's consultation (`complete_assignment`).
- `finalise` — make a task's deliverables meet its expected outputs   (`complete_assignment`), the task-level check after all steps + QA.

TcpAssignmentQaStatus.description: Outcome of a QA review — set by `assure_assignment`; null while not under (or before) review.

TcpAssignmentStatus.description: Lifecycle states for a  {@link  TcpAssignment } . A QA rejection returns the assignment from `in-qa` to `in-progress` (`qaStatus`/`qaFeedback` are cleared on that re-entry; `qaAttempts` is never reset).

TcpAssignmentWorkingArtifact.description: An artifact living in an assignment's own working directory, or inline text.

TcpCompany.description: Represents a company (tenant) within the LCP simulation. Each company has its own isolated set of agents, memory, and resources.

companyContext.description:
Optional company context injected as prompt part 2 at agent start. Describes the company environment: agent roster, shared storage layout, company name and description, and any company-wide behavioural guidelines.

When null, part 2 is omitted from the agent prompt.

embeddingConfig.description:
Provider and model configuration used for generating and querying embeddings. Must point to an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint (e.g. LM Studio `/v1/embeddings`, OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`).

When null, the RAG index and retrieval services are disabled for this company. Stored as JSONB — same shape as  {@link  LlmConfig }  but the `contextWindow` field is ignored.

id.description: Auto-generated primary key for this company.

llmConfig.description: Optional company-wide default LLM configuration. Roles that do not specify their own  {@link  TcpRole.llmConfig }  fall back to this value at run time, then to the environment-configured LLM fallback (`LLM_PROVIDER` / `LLM_MODEL`), before failing. Resolved via  {@link  LlmConfigResolver  } .

mcpServerList.description: Additional MCP server identifiers made available to every agent in this company, on top of the system's default servers and any extras listed on the running role. Additive, not a precedence override — resolved via  {@link  resolveMcpServerList  } .

name.description: Human-readable display name for the company.

nextTaskShortcodeIndex.description: Monotonically incrementing counter used to generate each new  {@link  TcpTask.shortcode  }  (`nextTaskShortcodeIndex` at generation time, then incremented). Incremented atomically (raw SQL `UPDATE … RETURNING` on PostgreSQL) — see `TaskService.create`.

plannerRole.description: Company-default planner role, used by  {@link  TcpTask.plannerRole  }  when a task does not specify its own. Must belong to this company — enforced at write time by `DbService`/`ApiService`, not by the FK alone.

runConfig.description: Optional company-wide agent-loop resource overrides. Applied when the running role has no  {@link  TcpRole.runConfig }  set. See  {@link  AgentRunConfig }  for available fields.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier used in API paths and agent namespacing. Must be globally unique across all companies.

systemPromptTemplate.description: Optional company-wide default `systemPromptTemplate`. Used when a role does not specify its own  {@link  TcpRole.systemPromptTemplate } ; falls back to `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE` when neither is set. Resolved via  {@link  SystemPromptTemplateResolver  } .

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. `'Europe/London'`) used only for *display* and prompt localization — CLI/UI timestamp formatting, and the `{{timezone}}`/ `{{localDatetime}}` prompt variables (see `buildPromptDateVars`). Never used for storage (always UTC) or as a replacement for the UTC time given to the LLM (`{{datetime}}` remains the authoritative anchor).

TcpMaterialArtifact.description: An artifact usable as task materials: an uploaded file, a promoted assignment output, or inline text.

TcpRole.description: A role template that defines the behaviour and LLM configuration for an agent. Multiple  {@link  TcpAgent  }  instances can run from the same role within a company.

company.description: The company this role belongs to.

companyId.description: Foreign key column for the owning  {@link  TcpCompany } .

description.description: Human-readable description of what this role does and what outputs it is expected to produce.

id.description: Auto-generated primary key for this role.

knowledgeDomains.description: Knowledge domain tags that will be used for RAG retrieval once the memory system is built. Stored now so roles can be defined ahead of the RAG implementation. ponytail: unused for MVP; consumed by the RAG phase

llmConfig.description: LLM provider and model configuration for agents running in this role. Stored as JSONB. When absent, resolved via  {@link  LlmConfigResolver  }  against  {@link  TcpCompany.llmConfig } , then the environment fallback.

mcpServerList.description: List of MCP server identifiers this role is permitted to call. Stored now; wired to the agent loop once MCP servers are implemented. ponytail: unused for MVP; consumed by the MCP integration phase

name.description: Short identifier for this role within the company (e.g. `'analyst'`, `'planner'`).

queryIndex.description: Monotonically incrementing counter used to generate unique  {@link  Conversation  }  slugs. Incremented atomically (raw SQL `UPDATE … RETURNING`) on each new conversation.

rolePrompt.description:
Optional role prompt injected as prompt part 1 immediately after the system prompt. Covers role identity, attitude, domain knowledge, and behavioural guidelines that are distinct from the system-level instructions.

When null, part 1 is omitted —  {@link  systemPromptTemplate }  continues to serve as the sole pre-task context until a role prompt is explicitly set.

runConfig.description: Optional agent-loop resource overrides for agents running in this role. Takes precedence over  {@link  TcpCompany.runConfig }  and environment variables. See  {@link  AgentRunConfig }  for available fields.

slug.description: URL-safe identifier used to address this role without its UUID (e.g. in `lcp-cli` or agent-to-agent consultation). Unique **within the owning company** only — unlike  {@link  TcpCompany.slug } , which is unique globally, the same role slug may be reused across different companies.

systemPromptTemplate.description:
Handlebars-style prompt template injected as the system message at agent start. Optional — when blank, resolved via  {@link  SystemPromptTemplateResolver  }  against  {@link  TcpCompany.systemPromptTemplate } , then `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`.

Available variables: `{{name}}`, `{{description}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{datetime}}`, `{{timezone}}`, `{{localDatetime}}`, `{{companyId}}`, `{{roleId}}`. The latter two let the agent supply identifiers required by company- and role-scoped MCP tool calls.

TcpTask.description: A piece of work requested by a user. A planner agent turns a task into a plan — an ordered list of implement-mode  {@link  TcpAssignment  }  records (there is no separate plan entity; see `TcpAssignment.orderIndex`).

company.description: The company this task belongs to.

companyId.description: Foreign key for the owning  {@link  TcpCompany } .

completed.description: Set at finalisation: the artifacts actually produced by the task.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when this task was created.

expected.description: Artifacts the task is expected to produce.

failureReason.description: Why the task failed — planner failure, QA exhaustion, etc. Null unless `status` is `failed`.

materials.description:
Task materials supplied at creation or upload time — `task-materials-path` or `inline-text` artifacts only.

Uses `simple-json` (stored as TEXT) for cross-DB compatibility with SQLite unit tests.

plannerRole.description: Explicit planner role for this task. Falls back to  {@link  TcpCompany.plannerRoleId }  at start time when unset.

request.description: The user's statement of the work to be done.

shortcode.description: Short, per-company identifier assigned at creation (`'000'`, `'001'`, …) — see  {@link  TcpCompany.nextTaskShortcodeIndex } . Unique within the owning company only.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of this task.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last status or field update.

TcpTaskCompletedArtifact.description: An artifact promoted into a task's completed directory, or inline text.

TcpTaskStatus.description: Lifecycle states for a  {@link  TcpTask } . `planning` reflects an active planner dispatch; other transitions derive from the task's implement-mode assignments (see `deriveTaskStatus`).

VersionedEntity.description:
Abstract base for entities that require optimistic concurrency control.

TypeORM increments `version` on every `save()` and throws `OptimisticLockVersionMismatchError` when a stale version is detected, preventing lost updates under concurrent writes. Callers should wrap writes in  {@link  withOptimisticRetry  } .

Apply to entities with concurrent write patterns: multiple BullMQ workers, HTTP endpoints, or background tasks that can race on the same row.

WithEmbeddingConfig.description: Marks an entity as carrying an optional embedding configuration, so callers can resolve it uniformly (see  {@link  EmbeddingConfigResolver  } ) instead of reading `embeddingConfig` off a specific entity type.

WithLlmConfig.description: Marks an entity as carrying an optional LLM configuration, so callers can treat role/company objects uniformly when resolving precedence between them (see  {@link  LlmConfigResolver  } ) instead of reading differently-named fields per entity.

status.description: Current lifecycle state of this assignment.

buildAssignmentShortcode.$comment:
(
  taskShortcode: string,
  mode: TcpAssignmentMode,
  planIndex: number) => string

Current lifecycle state of this assignment.
